title: World atlas

chronology.label: Creation
chronology.detail: Opening date in the Ussher-based chronology used by Adams; Genesis does not supply a BC year.

chronology.label: The Flood
chronology.detail: Adams's placement of the Flood in his biblical chronology, beside the book's ancient vessel accounts.

chronology.label: Confusion of Tongues · dispersion
chronology.detail: The date Adams prints for the confusion and dispersion; it is not a dated start of tower construction.

chronology.label: Call of Abraham
chronology.detail: Adams's next useful waypoint for following the biblical narrative into later history.

chronology.label: Second Temple destroyed
chronology.detail: The story atlas's principal endpoint. Later writers and manuscript copies appear as source dates, not new primeval events.

rows.title: Akkadian period
rows.basis: Historical and material-culture period; dates are approximate.

rows.title: Old Kingdom, Dynasty 6
rows.basis: Estimated historical reign chronology; Pyramid Texts were inscribed in this period.

rows.title: Mature Harappan urban phase
rows.basis: Approximate regional phase from excavations and radiocarbon at Harappa; individual sites differ.

rows.title: Shimao walled settlement
rows.basis: Archaeological and calibrated radiocarbon dating of the Shimao site.

rows.title: Caral-Supe settlement
rows.basis: Site development range supported by the Caral-Supe Project's radiocarbon analysis.

rows.title: Stonehenge: altered stones
rows.basis: Archaeological construction phase: bluestones rearranged and Avenue connected to the Avon.

rows.title: Mawmluh Cave isotope excursion
rows.basis: Local speleothem isotope signal, from 4303 to 3888 years BP; 4200 BP (c. 2250 BCE) is the modeled midpoint selected for the formal boundary.

outsideWindow.title: Earlier on the physical timeline
outsideWindow.detail: Monumental enclosures erected by hunter-gatherer groups. Their date belongs to the site, independently of Adams's chronology.

method: The parallel bands show what was happening in each region at the same time. Adams's biblical placements, historical periods, radiocarbon ranges, and a measured cave proxy each carry their own dating method, named on the row. The date of a surviving text or a later copy is given on its source card as the date of the copy; the event the text describes has its own place on the chart.
